questions_and_answers.question: How is the perfect participle formed in Hindi according to the lesson?

answers.answer: By adding the auxiliary verb before the root
By adding सक after the root
By adding one of the gender-number endings आ, ए, ई, ईं to the verb root

questions_and_answers.question: What can be inserted between the verb root and the perfect participle ending?
If a verb root ends with आ or ओ, what is added before the आ ending?
Which set of endings corresponds to masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural and feminine plural?
What does the present auxiliary in the perfect participle construction indicate?

answers.answer: The action is far in the past
The action occurred recently or relates to the present
The action will occur in the future

questions_and_answers.question: In the construction for meeting someone, which postposition follows the person being met?
According to the lesson, how is the English 'see' used for meeting someone translated in Hindi?
When is the pronoun आप used as an extra-polite reference to a third person?

answers.answer: In formal contexts like newspapers or introductions

questions_and_answers.question: Which of the following examples shows how to politely introduce someone using आप?

answers.answer: आप से मिलिये, आप हैं श्री वर्मा !

questions_and_answers.question: What should students do regarding verbs that form their past tenses using the perfect participle?

answers.answer: Practice with verbs from the provided list or similar ones
Use any verb with these endings

articles.text:
Most of the past tenses use the 'perfect participle' which consists of the root of the verb plus one of the four gender-number endings आ, ए, ई, ईं.

मैं पहुँचा । I (man) arrived      मैं पहुँची । I (woman) arrived
आप पहुँचे । you (man) arrived    आप पहुँचीं । you (woman) arrived

सक may come between the main verb root and the ending. क्या आप नहीं आ सके ?

If the root ends with आ or ओ, य is added before the आ ending. Examples include आया (came) and सोया (slept). Other endings may be spelled with or without य; it is not pronounced.

आया आया or आये, आयी or आई

होना and जाना have different roots for the perfect participle:
हुआ, हुए, हुई, हुए (happened)
गया, गए, गई, गईं (went)

The perfect participle may be followed by an auxiliary verb. For example:
मैं गया हूँ । (I have gone)
वे पहुँची है । (She has arrived)

The present auxiliary shows that the action occurred in the very recent past or has some reference to the present. With the past auxiliary, the action is definitely in the past, not closely connected with the present.

Only a certain number of verbs form their past tenses this way. For the time being, practice with verbs from the provided list or others of the same kind that your teachers give you.

The verb मिलना was presented with meanings like get, receive, find: (Person) को (Thing) मिलता है — the person gets the thing. In a different construction, मिलना is used for meet:
(Person A) (Person B) से मिलता है — Person A meets Person B.

Examples:
मैं हमेशा शर्मा जी से इतवार को मिलता हूँ । (I always meet Mr. Sharma on Sunday.)
उषा जी रोज़ डॉक्टर से मिलती थीं । (Usha used to visit the doctor every day.)
जब वहाँ जायेंगे, तो क्या आप किसी से मिलेंगे ? (When you go there, will you meet somebody?)

In English we use 'see' in this sense ('I'll see you'); देखना is never used this way in Hindi.

आप usually means you, but it is occasionally used as an extra-polite way of referring to a third person. Newspapers often refer to the Prime Minister or the President this way. It is also used in introductions where extra courtesy is appropriate:
आप से मिलिये, आप हैं श्री वर्मा ! (I'd like you to meet Mr. Verma.)
इनसे मिलिये is also used.
